messages:
marta: Heads up — onboarding echidna/seraphim-6b-int4. Quick smoke shows reproducible token-shift / rotary-phase misalignment after ~800 tokens when using our converted tokenizer. Generation drifts (off-by-1 token IDs) and kvcache keys appear shifted.

kevin: Can you paste a tiny repro and the failing output?

marta: Repro (local):
```bash
PYTHONPATH=./python:./serving pytest tests/onboard/test_echidna_longctx.py -k int4_smoke -q
```
Failing snippet from model output (fp16 vs int4):
```
input tokens: [134, 7, 4521, 9, 88, ...]
fp16 next tokens: [78, 202, 11, 3, 0]
int4 next tokens:  [78, 202, 12, 3, 0]  # diverges at position 3 (token id +1)
```
Also dumped kvcache keys at gen step 4: `kvcache_key[:6] = [0x1f4, 0x2a0, 0x3b0, 0x400, 0x1f4, 0x2a0]` — suspicious repeat/aliasing.

sanjay: Two quick suspects: (1) vocab special token mapping (seraphim fork added a BOS sentinel) so token IDs are offset during conversion; (2) our int4 packing/unpacking path does an unsigned wrap when casting small types and that corrupts indices used for rotary index math.

ryan: :face_with_monocle: we saw a very similar symptom on orion-rt13b where phase-table indexing used an unsigned dtype after quant path. The mismatch only shows up on longctx (>1024) because earlier tokens get masked in caches.

marta: Confirmed mask: divergence starts once kv cache reuse kicks in (step ~4). I ran a quick diff between loader->token_map and tokenizer.vocab: `token_map[0:20] vs tokenizer._ids[:20]` and they differ by +1 after index 3.

kevin: Try these quick checks: (A) dump tokenizer.special_tokens_map and tokenizer.vocab_size (B) run conversion with `--preserve-offsets` and compare token id stream before/after, (C) in kvcache path cast token ids as signed int: `tid = np.int32(tid) - vocab_offset` before using as index, and (D) ensure rotary phase table is computed in float32 (`phase_table = phase_table.astype(np.float32)`) before any fp16 quant ops.

marta: Running (A)/(B) now. Quick output: `special_tokens_map = {"bos": "<s>", "eos": "</s>"}` and `vocab_size = 50265` on converted model, but original repo had 50264. So there is indeed an extra sentinel. Conversion command I used: `model-convert --from=hf --to=redwood --quant=int4` (no preserve flag).

ci-bot: CI: test/regressions/echidna_longctx_int4 — FAILED (bleu: fp16=0.42, int4=0.30) — investigating.

sanjay: That extra vocab entry explains the +1. We need conversion to emit a mapping file (`vocab_offset`) and the loader must subtract it when building index->embed maps. Also verify any hardcoded sentinel indices in tokenizer code.

marta: Quick patch attempt: in converter add `--preserve-offsets` and write `vocab_offset.json` with `{ "offset": 1 }`. Re-run conversion + serve local patch that subtracts offset at kvcache index time.

marta: After patch (local): int4 BLEU improved to 0.39 (vs 0.42 fp16). Remaining discrepancy seems tied to rotary phase precision — int4 path was computing rotation angles in fp16 and then quantizing internal tables. Switching to compute phase tables in fp32 and cast down when used fixes the last ~70% of gap.

kevin: Nice. Follow-ups: (1) add a conversion validation step that compares token streams (first 2k tokens) between hf->converted mapping, (2) add unit to ensure kvcache indexing using signed ints, (3) add a small regression test for longctx generation in CI (we already saw it).

ryan: Also document the "vocab offset" case in the model-onboarding checklist — some forks append sentinels. Might be worth adding an automated sanity assert: `assert tokenizer.vocab_size == len(tokenizer.get_vocab())` after conversion.

marta: Will open PR with converter change + loader guard + CI regression. Posting short patch link: https://git.internal/redwood/conv/pulls/1423

ci-bot: PR 1423: running presubmit — conversion smoke + longctx-int4 bench queued.

marta: Thanks all — keeping this thread for triage notes. Will mark as resolved if presubmit passes.
